subtopic: Application of Logic to Switching Circuits
context: Q.12. Express the following circuits in the symbolic form. Prepare the switching table.
solution: Three branches in parallel. Top branch: \(S_1\) in series with \(S_2\), i.e. \(S_1 \wedge S_2\). Middle branch: \(S_1'\). Bottom branch: \(S_1\) in series with \(S_2'\), i.e. \(S_1 \wedge S_2'\). Symbolic form: \((S_1 \wedge S_2) \vee S_1' \vee (S_1 \wedge S_2')\).

subtopic: Application of Logic to Switching Circuits
context: Q.12. Express the following circuits in the symbolic form. Prepare the switching table.
solution: Two blocks in series. First block: \(S_1\) in parallel with \(S_2\), i.e. \(S_1 \vee S_2\). Second block: \(S_1\) in parallel with \(S_3\), i.e. \(S_1 \vee S_3\). Symbolic form: \((S_1 \vee S_2) \wedge (S_1 \vee S_3)\).

subtopic: Application of Logic to Switching Circuits
context: Q.13. Simplify the following so that the new circuit has minimum number of switches. Also, draw the simplified circuit.
solution: Three branches in parallel. Top: \(S_1 \wedge S_2'\); middle: \(S_1' \wedge S_2\); bottom: \(S_1' \wedge S_2'\). Symbolic form: \((S_1 \wedge S_2') \vee (S_1' \wedge S_2) \vee (S_1' \wedge S_2')\). Simplify: \((S_1 \wedge S_2') \vee [S_1' \wedge (S_2 \vee S_2')] = (S_1 \wedge S_2') \vee S_1'\). Since \(S_1 \vee S_1' \equiv\) all values, \((S_1 \wedge S_2') \vee S_1' \equiv S_1' \vee S_2'\). Simplified circuit: \(S_1'\) in parallel with \(S_2'\) (2 switches).

subtopic: Application of Logic to Switching Circuits
context: Q.13. Simplify the following so that the new circuit has minimum number of switches. Also, draw the simplified circuit.
solution: Two blocks in series. First block (parallel): \((S_1 \wedge S_2) \vee S_3' \vee S_4' \vee S_5'\). Second block (parallel): \((S_1 \wedge S_2) \vee (S_3 \wedge S_4 \wedge S_5)\). Symbolic form: \([(S_1 \wedge S_2) \vee S_3' \vee S_4' \vee S_5'] \wedge [(S_1 \wedge S_2) \vee (S_3 \wedge S_4 \wedge S_5)]\). Let \(a = S_1 \wedge S_2\), \(b = S_3 \wedge S_4 \wedge S_5\). First block \(= a \vee \sim b\) (since \(S_3' \vee S_4' \vee S_5' \equiv \sim(S_3 \wedge S_4 \wedge S_5) = \sim b\)). Expression \(= (a \vee \sim b) \wedge (a \vee b) = a \vee (\sim b \wedge b) = a \vee F = a = S_1 \wedge S_2\). Simplified circuit: \(S_1\) in series with \(S_2\) (2 switches).

subtopic: Application of Logic to Switching Circuits
context: Q.14. Check whether the following switching circuits are logically equivalent - Justify.
solution: Two blocks in series. First block: single switch \(S_1\). Second block: \(S_2\) in parallel with \(S_3\). Symbolic form: \(S_1 \wedge (S_2 \vee S_3)\).

subtopic: Application of Logic to Switching Circuits
context: Q.14. Check whether the following switching circuits are logically equivalent - Justify.
solution: Two branches in parallel. Top branch: \(S_1\) in series with \(S_2\), i.e. \(S_1 \wedge S_2\). Bottom branch: \(S_1\) in series with \(S_3\), i.e. \(S_1 \wedge S_3\). Symbolic form: \((S_1 \wedge S_2) \vee (S_1 \wedge S_3)\). By distributive law \(= S_1 \wedge (S_2 \vee S_3)\), which equals circuit i. Hence the two circuits in (A) are logically equivalent.

subtopic: Application of Logic to Switching Circuits

solution: Two blocks in series. First block: \(S_1\) in parallel with \(S_2\), i.e. \(S_1 \vee S_2\). Second block: \(S_1\) in parallel with \(S_3\), i.e. \(S_1 \vee S_3\). Symbolic form: \((S_1 \vee S_2) \wedge (S_1 \vee S_3)\).

subtopic: Application of Logic to Switching Circuits
context: Q.14. Check whether the following switching circuits are logically equivalent - Justify.
solution: Two branches in parallel. Top branch: single switch \(S_1\). Bottom branch: \(S_2\) in series with \(S_3\), i.e. \(S_2 \wedge S_3\). Symbolic form: \(S_1 \vee (S_2 \wedge S_3)\). By distributive law \((S_1 \vee S_2) \wedge (S_1 \vee S_3) = S_1 \vee (S_2 \wedge S_3)\), which equals circuit i. Hence the two circuits in (B) are logically equivalent.

subtopic: Application of Logic to Switching Circuits
context: Q.15. Give alternative arrangement of the following switching circuit, so that the new circuit has minimum switches.
solution: Four branches in parallel, each a series of three switches. Row 1: \(S_1 \wedge S_2 \wedge S_1'\); Row 2: \(S_1' \wedge S_2 \wedge S_3\); Row 3: \(S_1 \wedge S_2 \wedge S_3\); Row 4: \(S_1 \wedge S_2' \wedge S_3\). Symbolic form: \((S_1 \wedge S_2 \wedge S_1') \vee (S_1' \wedge S_2 \wedge S_3) \vee (S_1 \wedge S_2 \wedge S_3) \vee (S_1 \wedge S_2' \wedge S_3)\). Row 1 has \(S_1 \wedge S_1' \equiv F\), so it drops. Remaining: \((S_1' \wedge S_2 \wedge S_3) \vee (S_1 \wedge S_2 \wedge S_3) \vee (S_1 \wedge S_2' \wedge S_3)\). Take \(S_3\) common: \(S_3 \wedge [(S_1' \wedge S_2) \vee (S_1 \wedge S_2) \vee (S_1 \wedge S_2')]\). First two give \(S_2 \wedge (S_1' \vee S_1) \equiv S_2\); so bracket \(= S_2 \vee (S_1 \wedge S_2') = S_2 \vee S_1\). Simplified: \(S_3 \wedge (S_1 \vee S_2)\) — \(S_3\) in series with (\(S_1\) parallel \(S_2\)), 3 switches.

subtopic: Application of Logic to Switching Circuits
context: Q.16. Simplify the following circuit so that the new circuit has minimum number of switches.
solution: Three branches in parallel, each a series of two switches. Branch 1: \(S_1' \wedge S_2\); Branch 2: \(S_1 \wedge S_2'\); Branch 3: \(S_1 \wedge S_2\). Symbolic form: \((S_1' \wedge S_2) \vee (S_1 \wedge S_2') \vee (S_1 \wedge S_2)\). Group last two: \(S_1 \wedge (S_2' \vee S_2) \equiv S_1\). So expression \(= (S_1' \wedge S_2) \vee S_1 = S_1 \vee S_2\) (by \((S_1' \wedge S_2) \vee S_1 \equiv S_1 \vee S_2\)). Simplified circuit: \(S_1\) in parallel with \(S_2\) (2 switches).

subtopic: Application of Logic to Switching Circuits
context: Q.17. Represent the following switching circuit in symbolic form and construct its switching table. Write your conclusion from the switching table.
solution: Two blocks in series. First block: three switches in parallel \(S_1\), \(S_2'\), \(S_3'\), i.e. \(S_1 \vee S_2' \vee S_3'\). Second block: \(S_1\) in parallel with (\(S_2\) in series with \(S_3\)), i.e. \(S_1 \vee (S_2 \wedge S_3)\). Symbolic form: \((S_1 \vee S_2' \vee S_3') \wedge [S_1 \vee (S_2 \wedge S_3)]\). Conclusion from the switching table: the lamp glows for the combinations where this expression is true.
